I went through a period like that six years ago with my now wife. So many things going on, so many things to do, and so many things going wrong. It looked a lot like your life.

What helps me is to create a shared document online where we list the things that need to be done and keep them in coarse priority order. Things get added to the end and sometimes moved up, sometimes not. We don't always work on what is at the top of the list - that would be too rigid. Some days you don't feel like doing X, or it's an outdoor task on a bad day, etc. But having it on a list helps me to not keep going over and over the list in my head at night while trying to sleep.

I sometimes have another secret list - Things that are worrying me. That's for when I feel overwhelmed and don't know why. Usually, that list lives for a day or so. Once I have it all down, I can tell what it is that is most gnawing at me. It's the not knowing that is painful.

In times like this, it is sometimes better to deal with the task at hand than the whole picture. Make sure you are pointing out how helpful your husband is being and that you understand that he is under a lot of stress too. Make a dinner out night or go to a hotel room for a night.
